topic: No guided on-ramp into a new genre
unmet_need: Staged, goal-based exploration that coaches you into a genre
example_quotes: As an aspirational explorer I save tons of new music and forget all of it. Retention and rotation are the real unmet need.
Not deserve a single star I selected zeher movie playlist after completion 1song it plays rab ne bana di jodi..
New music never sticks for me. I play a recommended song once and forget it it never makes it into my rotation.
trying to get into jazz but i keep bouncing off it. i need a guided on-ramp not a 5 hour playlist someone help
Guided genre missions get into jazz over 3 weeks with a staged on-ramp would be a game changer for beginners.
Busy mom, two kids, I want new music that fits my existing taste delivered to me with zero effort. I will not go digging. Bring it to me.
Texas Music Supporter. Its nice to be able to have my favorite artist and their music at my fingertips!
as a busy parent i have zero time to crate dig. i just want good new music to come to me with no effort

unmet_need: A clear bridge explaining why a track fits your existing taste
example_quotes: Honestly when a recommendation explains why a track fits my taste, I trust it so much more. The 'why' is everything.
Its doesnt. Doesnt even let you go back and when u have a playlist it doesnt go To the next song from your playlist
Discovery is a one shot thing. There's no sense of progress, no goal, no feeling that I'm actually growing my taste over time.
Grounded 'why this' bridges build trust. Recommendations without a reason feel random and I never act on them.
Recommendations feel random and disconnected from my taste. There's no thread connecting the new song to what I actually listen to.
it is something like mind fresh and there are so many songs if you like song so you do this download this
the recs never tell me WHY a song was picked. i don't trust a recommendation that comes with no reason
Recommended songs. Keeps playing recommended songs that I do not like and I will like it to stop and just keep playing songs in my playlist

topic: Stuck in a listening loop / same songs on repeat
unmet_need: Gentle nudges that expand the rotation without losing comfort
research_question: Q4 repeat-listening of the same content
example_quotes: The same 50 songs on repeat problem is so real. I love them but I'm in a loop and the app does nothing to gently expand it.
Stuck-in-a-loop is so real. People fall back on the same songs on repeat; the product that breaks that rut wins.
Honestly I listen to the same 50 songs on repeat. I want new music but I have zero energy to go looking for it after work and kids.
stuck in a rut listening to the same songs on repeat and the algorithm refuses to break me out of the loop
give me a dial for how adventurous my recs are. some days i want comfort, some days i want a real stretch
I used to crate dig for hours. After kids I just loop the same comfort songs. I miss discovering but the effort barrier is too high now.
Stuck on repeat with the same comfort songs. The app never gently nudges me to expand my rotation.
There's no reinforcement loop. I discover an artist, play them once, and then they vanish from my life because nothing brings them back at the right moment.

unmet_need: Genuinely novel recommendations that expand taste, not reinforce it
example_quotes: A comfort-to-curiosity dial is genius. The biggest gap in every recommender is control over how far the recs stretch.
Power digger here. I want deep cuts and obscure artists below a certain popularity, but the algorithm plays it way too safe.
The killer feature would be adoption tracking. Most discovery never converts into a lasting habit a first play is not a win.
The algorithm is too cautious. I'd love a slider for how adventurous the recommendations are, from safe to totally out there.
Same here. The algorithm keeps recommending the same five artists over and over. It feels like an echo chamber, not discovery.
I just want a control slider comfort versus curiosity instead of a fixed algorithm deciding how adventurous I get.
discover weekly used to find me artists i'd never have found myself. now it's all safe picks i already know. discovery is broken
I open Discover Weekly, save a couple songs, and forget them by next week. High intent, nothing sticks. Story of my Spotify life.

topic: Discovery surfaces don't lead anywhere new
unmet_need: Discovery that introduces artists you'd never have found yourself
example_quotes: More Discovery Tracks. There needs to be more discovery tracks. When I ask for more it plays the same songs Ive heard before
why do i save 10 songs off release radar and then never listen to them again. nothing ever sticks lol
Discovery is overwhelming. There's too much music and no good way to ease into something new. I just give up and put on my liked songs again.

Atrocious Shuffle and Playlists. Spotify has the worst shuffle for Liked Songs. I hear the same songs day after day, and I have 1,499 songs liked. Their playlists are so generic too. Always having songs I already like. Its the worst place to find new music/artists Ive never heard before. Seems to be heavily based on what label artists are on. Please fix. Thanks.

Enable DJ for Discover Weekly and Release Radar. I love the idea of DJ, but don't like, yet again, how repetitive it is, in that it plays you things you already know. (Note: our culture is bigger than two pieces of music.) I do LOVE your Discover Weekly and Release Radar features though, so it would be lovely to have these two playlists, but with the DJ talking in between

Feature request: Hide already liked songs from Release Radar. Please add an option to hide songs from Release Radar that Ive already liked/saved. I use Release Radar specifically to discover new releases. Seeing songs Ive already listened to and saved makes it harder to find the genuinely new tracks. A simple **Hide liked songs** filter would make Release Radar much more useful

Spotify App quitting mid song. Hey @Jake5194 , Thanks for getting back to us. There isn't a specific threshold we can guarantee, but we'd suggest reducing your Liked Songs to around 10,000 tracks and seeing if that improves things. We're also aware of some performance issues that can affect larger libraries, and the relevant team is currently working on improvements. In the meantime, keeping the library closer to 10,000 tracks is our best recommendation. Cheers,

[Discover Weekly] Mark which songs Ive listened to. It concerns Discover Weekly and Release Radar. I would love to know which songs Ive listened to or not in the playlist. Some songs are not bad enough to dislike but not good enough to like. And if I dont go through the playlist at once, I could end up listening to a song Ive listened to already and not discover a new one (which is the goal). I would love an indicator that shows when the song has been listened to more than 50% so I can focus on the other ones before the playlist resets itself.
